sections.h2: What does the Tacoma housing market look like to a seller?
sections.html:
Tacoma homeowners report a median home value of $479,600 in the Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates, and 55.8 percent of households own rather than rent. The city is the county seat of Pierce County and the economic center of the South Sound region, with an estimated 229,816 residents on July 1, 2025.

The median gross rent of $1,676 matters if you own a house that tenants occupy. Tacoma households earn a median of $85,884, and workers spend an average of 28.8 minutes getting to their jobs. Joint Base Lewis-McChord lies several miles south of the city, and Seattle-Tacoma International Airport is 22 miles north in SeaTac.

sections.h2: Which Tacoma neighborhoods do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Buyers tend to ask which part of town a house is in before anything else. The city is grouped into Central Tacoma, New Tacoma around downtown, North Tacoma, Northeast Tacoma, West Tacoma and the Port of Tacoma area, and each carries its own character.

  • Central Tacoma includes Hilltop, Delong Park, the Wedge, Bryant and College Heights.
  • North Tacoma includes the Proctor District, the North Slope, Old Tacoma, Ruston Way, Skyline and Yakima Hill.
  • West Tacoma includes the Highlands, Narrows, Titlow and Salmon Beach.
  • Downtown takes in the Stadium District, the Theater District, the Dome District and the Thea Foss Waterway.

Transit shapes demand around the core. Sound Transit runs the T Line between Tacoma Dome Station, downtown, the University of Washington Tacoma campus and Hilltop, and also operates Sounder trains and express buses toward Seattle. Most of the city belongs to Tacoma Public Schools, which lists 36 elementary schools, 11 middle schools and 10 high schools, including Stadium High School and Mount Tahoma High School. Ruston is a separately incorporated town and Browns Point is unincorporated, so confirm which jurisdiction your parcel sits in before you ask the City of Tacoma about permits. Tacoma also keeps a historic preservation program with 165 city landmarks and more than 1,000 historic properties across five overlay zones, so ask the city whether your older home sits in one before you plan exterior work.

sections.h2: How do Tacoma's land, water and climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Elevation and shoreline do most of the work. The city ranges from sea level to roughly 500 feet and covers 62.34 square miles, of which 12.62 square miles are water, and it wraps around Commencement Bay on Puget Sound. Many parts of the city have views of Mount Rainier, and the low-lying ground near the Port of Tacoma sits in the path of a lahar from the Puyallup River if the volcano ever erupts.

Tacoma has a warm-summer Mediterranean climate, with July and August the warmest months and December the coldest. Mean daily highs run 48.1 degrees in January and 76.9 in August. The industrial tide flats once produced the odor known as the Tacoma Aroma, which ended when the Simpson Tacoma Kraft mill closed in September 2023.

The Port of Tacoma is among the largest seaports in the Pacific Northwest, and a refinery has operated on the tide flats since 1952. Downtown has been revitalized since the 1990s, with the University of Washington Tacoma campus, the T Line and a restored Thea Foss Waterway. The Tacoma Narrows bridges connect the city to Gig Harbor and the Kitsap Peninsula.

sections.h2: What property maintenance changes are coming for Tacoma owners?
sections.html:
Tacoma adopted a new property maintenance standard that takes effect on January 1, 2027. The City Council passed Ordinance 29125, which brings International Property Maintenance Code standards into the city's Property Maintenance and Nuisance Code and strengthens the tools the city uses against repeat and chronic violations.

The city says it handles roughly 4,500 property maintenance cases a year under older rules in Chapters 8.30 and 2.01 of its code. Section 7 of the ordinance states that the expanded enforcement program becomes operational no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so the day-to-day effect depends on future budget decisions. If you own a vacant, neglected or rental house in Tacoma, find out whether any open code complaint is attached to it, and read the details at tacoma.gov/IPMC. Ask the city for any open complaint on the property before you list.

sections.h2: What taxes and disclosures come with a Tacoma sale?
sections.html:
Pierce County bills and collects property tax for Tacoma addresses through the Assessor-Treasurer's office at 2401 S. 35th St., Room 142, in Tacoma, reachable at (253) 798-6111. The second-half 2026 payment deadline was November 2, so a closing now should settle any unpaid balance and prorate the part of the year that the buyer will own. Payments can be made online through the parcel search site, by phone at (253) 798-3333, by mail to Pierce County Finance, or at the cashier lobby at 1501 Market St., Suite 120, from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Newer exemption rules also matter: starting in January 2027 more Pierce County homeowners who are 61 or older, or who have a qualifying disability, will see their taxes reduced under an expanded state program.

Real estate excise tax is due from the seller at the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state portion is 1.1 percent on the first $525,000 of the price and 1.28 percent on the amount between $525,000 and $1,525,000, and a local portion is added. Under RCW 64.06.020, a seller of most improved residential property must deliver a signed disclosure statement within five business days after the buyer and seller sign a contract. The form includes questions about the roof, plumbing, electrical and heating systems, and it notes that the seller must provide carbon monoxide alarms and at least one smoke detection device.

  • Gather your latest tax statement and any special assessments before listing.
  • Ask the county for the payoff amount on any unpaid taxes.
  • Collect permit records for additions, such as a converted garage or a new bathroom.
  • Check whether the city or the county has any open complaint or lien tied to the parcel.

sections.h2: Should I list my Tacoma house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
The answer turns on your repair budget, your calendar and how much work the house needs before a buyer's inspector walks through. A listing exposes the house to the open market. A cash offer trades some of that exposure for speed and fewer conditions, which suits a vacant house, an inherited property or a rental with a tenant in place.

Whichever route you choose, compare written offers on net proceeds, not on the headline price. Ask each buyer who pays the excise tax, how long the offer is open, what the closing date is and whether they accept the house as it stands with its contents.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Tacoma that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer may purchase the house as it stands, and on most residential sales you must complete the seller disclosure statement describing the property's condition to the best of your knowledge.

faqs.q: What does Ordinance 29125 mean for Tacoma sellers?
faqs.a: It sets a new property maintenance standard that takes effect January 1, 2027. The expanded enforcement program starts no earlier than nine months after the council funds it, so check for open code complaints on your property before you sell.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Tacoma house?
faqs.a: Pierce County does, through its Assessor-Treasurer's office in Tacoma. Call (253) 798-6111 for assessed values, statements and exemptions, and ask for a payoff figure before closing.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Tacoma house sells?
faqs.a: The seller usually pays it, and it is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. The state rate is graduated, starting at 1.1 percent on the first $525,000, with a local portion added.

faqs.q: How many people live in Tacoma?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 229,816 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 219,346 at the April 2020 census. Tacoma is the third most populous city in Washington.
